title: Performing shell arithmetic on a value not first validated as a number
purpose: Prevent a non-numeric or malicious-looking string from being reinterpreted by arithmetic (a typo'd or empty field can disable a bound or set a wild value), which an LLM wrongly treats as impossible.
trigger: A `(( ))`, `$(( ))`, or let expression or a `[ ]`/`[[ ]]` numeric comparison consumes a value with no preceding whitelist regex like ^[0-9]+$ that would have rejected non-digits.
correct: Before arithmetic or numeric comparison, validate the field is all-digits (e.g. [[ "$x" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]); reject or correct it when not. Guard a timeout/count as > 0 so a bad value cannot just disable the protection.
evidence_note: Grounded in bin/queue-dev-timeout rejecting a non-positive timeout before use and assets.d/queue.sh duration parsing; docs/SNMP_INTEGRATION.md validates with ^[0-9]+$ before arithmetic.
return_semantics: A reference rule page; shown for LLM author guidance, not executed by rules check.
